name: Avocado Green
lede: Avocado Green is a bright, yellow-green, and a color-name whose meaning shifts with whose avocado you picture.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines the avocado's green as the pulp rather than the skin, and traces the fruit's name to two possible roots, Spanish *abocado* or Aztec *ahuacatl* [1]. St Clair uses avocado green as an example of a name that may baffle readers a century on: skin, outer flesh or the butter tint near the seed [2].

The library carries the swatch from the xkcd survey and lists it in ISCC-NBS block 120 and Maerz and Paul [3]. Its nearest standard color is Kelly green, at a distance of 10.1 [3]. Close greens include [[apple-green]] and [[olive]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 6 paintings in our archive of 23,781 hold this color, 0.03% of them, as photographed [4]. In printed English the word peaks in the 2010s and rose fastest in the 2000s, but Google Books counts every sense of the word, including the fruit [4].

origin.named_after: the avocado fruit; its name perhaps from Spanish abocado or Aztec ahuacatl
origin.first_recorded: origin of the color name undocumented

questions.q: According to Paterson, which part of the avocado does its green usually refer to?
St Clair argues that names like avocado green will always stay clear to later readers.

openers: Paterson ties avocado green to the pulp, not the skin.
